translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
Shabbos Parshas Vayikra,
3rd of Nissan, 5732

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions why the call of affection precedes specifically the laws of offerings, indicating that the revelation of Torah is primarily in the laws of offerings.

translations.translation: "And He called to Moshe, and Hashem spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying: 'When a man from among you brings an offering to Hashem...'"
And it needs to be understood,
for to all speeches and all sayings and all commandments there preceded a call, an expression of affection,
so why was the call stated
(explicitly)
specifically in the portion of offerings?
Now, simply it can be said,
that what is written "And He called" in the portion of offerings is
because the beginning of speech from the Tent of Meeting was this portion.
But this itself requires explanation,
that the beginning of speech from the Tent of Meeting was specifically the portion of offerings.
And from this it is implied,
that the revelation of Torah
(the concept of the Tent of Meeting)
is primarily in the laws of offerings.
And it can be said,
that this is also that the book of Vayikra
(the book of offerings)
is the most stringent of the books.
And this is also that it is the third book of the five books of the Torah,
for the virtue of the Torah, that it is the "Third Light"
is more revealed in the laws of offerings of the Torah.
And this is also that this—that for all the speeches of the Torah a call, an expression of affection, preceded—is learned from what is written in the portion of offerings,
for also this virtue of the Torah, its primary revelation is in the laws of offerings.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the Zohar's teaching that Israel are called "Adam" due to their attachment to Hashem, which is the power behind offering sacrifices, distinguishing between the attachment of vessels and the essential attachment of lights.

translations.translation: And this can be explained based on what the Rebbe
(the Rebbe Rashab)
of blessed memory, whose yahrtzeit is on the 2nd of Nissan, said in his maamar beginning "Adam ki yakriv",
that seemingly it should have said "when you bring an offering"
without mentioning who is the one bringing the offering.
And he brings in the maamar,
that it is stated in the Zohar
"Fortunate are Israel that the Holy One, blessed be He, called them 'Adam'... 'When a man from among you brings an offering',
what is the reason He called them 'Adam'? Because it is written
'And you who cling to Hashem your God are all alive today.'"
And based on this he explains what is written "When a man brings an offering"
(specifically "Adam"),
for the power that Israel have
to bring offerings is because they are of the category of "Adam",
that they are attached to the Holy One, blessed be He.
And he continues in the maamar,
that similarly it is stated in the Midrash,
that this that the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded Israel to bring offerings is because they are attached to Me,
as it is written
"For just as a belt clings to a man's waist..."
And he explains in the maamar,
that the Midrash speaks about the matter of the attachment of vessels,
that vessels are
in the category of existence and unification
(the attachment)
of them is not an essential unification,
like "when a belt clings..." that the belt is an existence unto itself except that it is attached to the person,
and in the Zohar it speaks about the matter of the attachment of lights,
that the attachment and unification of lights is an essential unification,
and therefore it brings the verse "And you who cling to Hashem your God",
actual attachment.
